titlu: Accounting, in the order it happens
subtitlu: A book about Romanian accounting, organized not by textbook chapters but by the accounting cycle — the real journey of a sum, from the document received to the filed balance sheet.
teza: Textbooks teach accounting by topic: accounts, then VAT, then payroll. Practice doesn't work that way. A company goes through the same sequence every month, in the same order, and each step depends on the one before it.
The book follows the sequence. Each part is a phase of the cycle; each chapter answers a question you ask yourself at exactly that moment, not three months earlier.

Revised professional edition, with legislation verified as of August 27, 2026. Scope: Romanian entities applying the accounting regulations approved by OMFP no. 1.802/2014; IFRS treatments, the public sector, and non-profit organizations require distinct rules.

doua.txt: What happens to the documents they bring in, why they're required, and how to read the figures that come out at the end. No formulas.
The accounting treatment behind every transaction, the legal basis, and the checks that catch an error before it reaches a declaration.

parti.titlu: Why accounting looks the way it does
parti.rezumat: The part missing from most textbooks: what question all this work actually answers. Without it, the rest looks like bureaucracy.

capitole.titlu: Two questions, and neither about accounts
capitole.nota: How much did I earn? What do I have and to whom do I owe it? Everything that follows serves these two questions.

capitole.titlu: Why every sum is written twice
capitole.nota: Double-entry bookkeeping isn't a bureaucratic convention but a built-in check: every movement has a source and a destination.

capitole.titlu: The drawers: the chart of accounts
capitole.nota: Why 4111 means "customers" and 401 means "suppliers" — a vocabulary to learn, not a list to memorize.

capitole.titlu: Who is responsible for the figures
capitole.nota: The business owner brings the documents and knows the business. The accountant verifies, signs, and bears professional responsibility. Neither replaces the other.

capitole.titlu: The accounting cycle: the map of the book
capitole.nota: The fourteen phases, in the order they're carried out, and why the order isn't negotiable.

parti.rezumat: Done once a year and rarely revisited — but if it's wrong here, nothing that follows can be easily corrected.

capitole.nota: VAT payer or not, corporate income tax or micro-enterprise tax: this choice determines which declarations you owe all year.
Where you start from, when the company isn't in its first year. Taking over balances from another program, account by account.

capitole.titlu: The equality that must hold from day one
capitole.nota: Total debit = total credit. An unbalanced opening trial balance can never be closed.

parti.rezumat: The only entry point. The rule that organizes the whole book: nothing enters the accounts except through a supporting document.

capitole.nota: Why this rule isn't formalism, but the only guarantee that the figures can be defended in an audit.
Which account is debited, which is credited, with what amount — and how to read a journal entry without knowing the formula.
Over a hundred and twenty typical transactions, grouped by family: sales, purchases, treasury, payroll, fixed assets, adjustments.
The separation between who enters and who takes responsibility. Only what's posted enters the accounts.
Does the arithmetic add up? Is the rate correct? Is the period open? Is the partner known? Isn't the document already recorded?
Numbering, mandatory content, and the electronic file that goes out through the ANAF system.

parti.rezumat: The treasury account is the only one that can be checked against an outside reality: the bank statement. That's why it's also the best error detector.

capitole.nota: Receipts, payments, and why the cash balance may never be negative.
The accounts against the statement. What doesn't match is exactly what needs clarifying — the rest requires no attention.
The cash register, cash payments between companies, treasury advances: the thresholds that check themselves.

parti.titlu: What you have, what you produce, who works
parti.rezumat: The three categories that require their own records, beyond the accounts: goods, people, and things that are consumed over time.

capitole.nota: Inflows, outflows, warehouses. Weighted average cost or FIFO — what the choice changes in the month's result.

capitole.titlu: Production: from raw materials to finished product
capitole.nota: The recipe, the consumption, the production cost, and how it reaches inventory.
The moment when counted reality confronts the book records. Surpluses, shortfalls, charging responsibility, minutes of the count.
Gross, contributions, tax, net — and who pays each part: the employee or the company.

capitole.titlu: The rights you lose if you don't claim them
capitole.nota: The personal deduction, non-taxable amounts, leave. An unfilled field costs real money, every month.
How an asset is consumed over time, why its useful life isn't chosen at random, and what the official catalog says.
An installment that isn't a single expense: principal, interest, and VAT, each with its own path.

parti.titlu: What doesn't come from a document
parti.rezumat: The part textbooks cover in three pages and simple software skips entirely. Without it, the balance sheet looks fine — but isn't true.

capitole.nota: Entries that don't come from correspondence, but from the passage of time and economic reality.
Receivables and payables in foreign currency, brought to the closing exchange rate. The difference is revenue or expense, not a technical adjustment.
When the customer is late, when they stop paying altogether, and how the adjustment is reversed if they pay after all.
Insurance paid today for twelve months isn't this month's expense. Prepaid expenses and deferred revenue.
The correction is made through a reverse entry, which remains linked to the original one. The trace of the error is part of the proof — that's why it's written "in red," not erased.

parti.rezumat: The same transactions, viewed from two angles — and the tool that tells you whether everything holds together.

capitole.nota: Everything that happened, in the order it happened. The register the law requires first.
The same transactions, grouped by account. This is where every check starts: from the figure, back to the document that produced it.
Opening balance + turnover = closing balance, and total debit equal to total credit. If it doesn't close, you find out here — not at the balance sheet.
The most counterintuitive chapter in the book: a symmetrical error passes any balance check. What the trial balance catches, what it doesn't, and what must be checked differently.
Who owes you, whom you owe, and since when. The age of balances as a management tool, not just a reporting one.

parti.rezumat: What you owe, when, and how you prove you filed. The declaration isn't a form to fill in, but the result of a month already recorded.

capitole.nota: How the return is built from the month's transactions and why the balance naturally carries over from one month to the next.
Cash-basis VAT, pro-rata, reverse charge, the margin scheme, triangular transactions. When the general rule doesn't apply.
What a company owes depending on the chosen regime, from the VAT return to the annual financial statements.
The Virtual Private Space, the signature, the receipt. The document that matters isn't the declaration, but the confirmation that it was received.

parti.rezumat: The moment when the month or year becomes final. The order of steps matters, and skipping one only shows up months later.

capitole.titlu: Closing the month, step by step
capitole.nota: Documents complete, the statement reconciled, adjustments made, VAT settled, declarations filed.

capitole.titlu: Status is derived from data, not checked off
capitole.nota: Why a manual checkbox lies: it stays true even after the data underneath it has changed.
A closed month is not touched again. And if it must be, forcing it open requires a written reason that leaves a trace.
Revenues and expenses are extinguished in the profit-and-loss account. What "we closed the year" actually means.

capitole.titlu: From accounting result to taxable result
capitole.nota: The tax records register: which expenses aren't deductible, which revenues aren't taxed, and why tax isn't calculated from accounting profit.
The legal reserve, retained earnings, dividends and their tax. The last step of one fiscal year and the first of the next.

parti.rezumat: The documents all the rest was done for. They're generated from the same records — not composed separately.

capitole.nota: Did you earn or lose money in the year, and from what exactly: operating or financial activity.
What you have and what you owe on a specific date. Why the two sides are equal by construction, not by luck.
The cash flow statement, changes in equity, explanatory notes. What they say and why they aren't filed in the same file.

capitole.titlu: The four consistencies to check before signing
capitole.nota: Assets = liabilities and equity. The result on the balance sheet = the result on the income statement. Cash in the flow statement = the balance of the treasury accounts. The variation = the sum of the three activities.

parti.rezumat: What remains after everything is filed — and why this part matters exactly on the day someone starts asking questions.

capitole.nota: The month's file, the year's file, the legal retention periods. What "I have the documents" means when they're actually requested.
The operations log as an internal control tool, not a surveillance one.
Software calculates and checks. It doesn't decide whether an expense belongs to the company, doesn't sign the balance sheet, and doesn't take responsibility on anyone's behalf.

parti.rezumat: The area where accounting stops being data entry: choosing the treatment, making the estimate, assessing risk, documenting the conclusion, and reviewing a piece of work that must be defensible.

capitole.titlu: Accounting policies, estimates, errors and materiality
capitole.nota: How to separate a permitted choice from an estimate and from an error; prospective effect, correction through retained earnings, and documenting materiality.

capitole.titlu: Provisions, subsequent events, and going concern
capitole.nota: Present obligation, probability, reliable estimate, adjusting events, and the test through which the going-concern signature becomes a proven conclusion.

capitole.titlu: Related parties, shareholders, capital, and financing
capitole.nota: The economic substance of money flowing between the company and its shareholders, arm's-length conditions, net assets, dividends, and the restrictions applicable in 2026.
Assertions, evidence, thresholds, sampling, lead schedules, open points, and the conclusion that links the trial balance to the financial statements.

capitole.titlu: The chart of accounts, by class
capitole.nota: With plain-language explanations for the accounts a small company actually touches.
From a goods invoice to reactivating a lost receivable, each with the complete journal entry — generated from the application, not written by hand.
What's filed, by when, and by whom — by regime.
"Journal entry" means a recorded transaction. "To reverse" means to cancel correctly. Plus the everyday vocabulary of declarations.
The short list to run through before every filing, in the order that catches the most errors.
Official sources, their hierarchy, the volatile values as of August 27, 2026, and the procedure by which the book stays current without mistaking a press release for the law.

subsol.txt: 12 parts, 55 chapters, 6 annexes. The first 11 parts follow the accounting cycle; part XII documents the professional judgment that runs through all the phases.

The base text is written for someone with no accounting background. Where the subject requires it, the chapter continues with the treatment, the legal basis, and the corresponding check, marked separately, so the two readings don't get mixed up.

Chapters 29 and 33 are the ones I would write first: “you reverse it, you don't delete it” and “balanced doesn't mean correct.” Both go against intuition, and both explain errors that go unnoticed for months on end.
